name: Luca Giordano
findings: Uses smoky black 1.4x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 916 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, buff turns up as a small accent in 100% of the paintings that hold it, 2.4x the archive's rate (from 916 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, deep space sparkle turns up as the lightest note in 60% of the paintings that hold it, 2.7x the archive's rate (from 916 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, cameo brown turns up as the shadow in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 1.9x the archive's rate (from 916 paintings here).
Pairs madder blue with plumbago grey more than chance would predict (3 of 916 paintings here).
Pairs dusty rose brown with mauve brown more than chance would predict (3 of 916 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, dark walnut, bistre) covers 62% of his paintings here.
Keeps 2 distinct palette families here, from smoky black, dark walnut to smoky black, bistre.
